about: Packet events: the names and meanings of the TCP events the capture reader reports, and the TLS names it decodes (versions, handshake messages, alerts, cipher suites). copy_window_ms is how close in time two identical packets must be to count as one packet logged at two pktmon components; out_of_order_ms is how soon after the newest data an earlier, unseen segment counts as out of order rather than retransmitted; events_shown_per_kind is how many of each kind are listed; the keep-alives of one connection direction are listed as one event, which counts once toward that limit.

tls13.title: RFC 8446: The Transport Layer Security (TLS) Protocol Version 1.3

events.name: Retransmission
events.meaning: A segment was sent again because it was not acknowledged in time.

events.name: Fast retransmission
events.meaning: A segment was sent again after the receiver reported it missing with duplicate ACKs.

events.name: Spurious retransmission
events.meaning: A segment was sent again although the receiver had already acknowledged it.

events.name: Out-of-order
events.meaning: A segment arrived after a later one.

events.name: Previous segment not captured
events.meaning: Data before this segment is missing from the capture: lost on the network, or not captured.

events.name: Duplicate ACK
events.meaning: The receiver acknowledged the same data again, which reports a gap in what it received.

events.name: Keep-alive
events.meaning: An idle connection was checked to see whether the other side is still there.

events.name: Reset
events.meaning: The connection was ended at once (RST), or a connection attempt was refused.

events.name: Zero window
events.meaning: The sender of this packet could take no more data until its application read what it had.

events.name: TLS alert
events.meaning: A TLS alert: a fatal alert ends the session; close_notify is a normal close.

tls_alerts.name: close_notify
tls_alerts.meaning: The session is being closed normally.

tls_alerts.name: unexpected_message
tls_alerts.meaning: A message arrived that was not expected at that point.

tls_alerts.name: bad_record_mac
tls_alerts.meaning: A record failed its integrity check.

tls_alerts.name: decryption_failed
tls_alerts.meaning: A record could not be decrypted.

tls_alerts.name: record_overflow
tls_alerts.meaning: A record was longer than allowed.

tls_alerts.name: decompression_failure
tls_alerts.meaning: A record could not be decompressed.

tls_alerts.name: handshake_failure
tls_alerts.meaning: The two sides found no protocol version, cipher suite or settings they both accept.

tls_alerts.name: no_certificate
tls_alerts.meaning: No certificate was sent when one was requested.

tls_alerts.name: bad_certificate
tls_alerts.meaning: The certificate is damaged or its signature does not verify.

tls_alerts.name: unsupported_certificate
tls_alerts.meaning: The certificate is of a type the peer does not accept.

tls_alerts.name: certificate_revoked
tls_alerts.meaning: The certificate was revoked by its issuer.

tls_alerts.name: certificate_expired
tls_alerts.meaning: The certificate has expired or is not yet valid.

tls_alerts.name: certificate_unknown
tls_alerts.meaning: The certificate could not be accepted for another reason.

tls_alerts.name: illegal_parameter
tls_alerts.meaning: A handshake field held a value that is not allowed.

tls_alerts.name: unknown_ca
tls_alerts.meaning: The peer does not trust the authority that issued the certificate.

tls_alerts.name: access_denied
tls_alerts.meaning: The peer refused the connection after checking access.

tls_alerts.name: decode_error
tls_alerts.meaning: A message could not be decoded.

tls_alerts.name: decrypt_error
tls_alerts.meaning: A handshake check failed, such as a signature or the Finished message.

tls_alerts.name: export_restriction
tls_alerts.meaning: An export-restricted setting was refused.

tls_alerts.name: protocol_version
tls_alerts.meaning: The peer does not accept the TLS version offered.

tls_alerts.name: insufficient_security
tls_alerts.meaning: The peer requires stronger cipher suites than were offered.

tls_alerts.name: internal_error
tls_alerts.meaning: The peer failed for a reason of its own, not caused by the other side.

tls_alerts.name: inappropriate_fallback
tls_alerts.meaning: A retry with a lower TLS version was refused.

tls_alerts.name: user_canceled
tls_alerts.meaning: The handshake was cancelled.

tls_alerts.name: no_renegotiation
tls_alerts.meaning: A renegotiation request was refused.

tls_alerts.name: missing_extension
tls_alerts.meaning: A required extension was not sent.

tls_alerts.name: unsupported_extension
tls_alerts.meaning: An extension was sent that the peer did not offer.

tls_alerts.name: unrecognized_name
tls_alerts.meaning: The server has no certificate for the name the client asked for.

tls_alerts.name: bad_certificate_status_response
tls_alerts.meaning: The certificate status (OCSP) response was not valid.

tls_alerts.name: unknown_psk_identity
tls_alerts.meaning: The pre-shared key identity is not known.

tls_alerts.name: certificate_required
tls_alerts.meaning: The server requires a client certificate and none was sent.

tls_alerts.name: no_application_protocol
tls_alerts.meaning: No application protocol (ALPN) both sides accept.
